The `CompatibleFunctions` structure contains a `FunctionDistances` $\mathbb R\,X$ structure: a type $\Theta(X)$ with an injective map from $\Theta(X)$ to the continuous functions $X	o\mathbb R$ (we apply $\vartheta\in\Theta(X)$ to points of $X$ through it) and, for each $x\in X$ and $r\in\mathbb R$, a pseudometric $d_{x,r}$ on $\Theta(X)$ (with extended version $ ar d_{x,r}$); it also asserts the existence of a point of $X$ at which every element of $\Theta(X)$ vanishes, plus the further compatibility axioms of `CompatibleFunctions`. e y'\in B(x,r)}|\varphi(y)-\varphi(y')|/d(y,y')\in[0,\infty]$. u(x,y)=K(x,y)\,\psi(D^{-
u}d(x,y))$ for $
u\in\mathbb Z$ (`Ks`), and $\psi(r)=\max(0,\min(1,4Dr-1,2-4r))$ for $r\in\mathbb R$; and for a set of tiles $\mathfrak C\subseteq\mathfrak P$ let $T^*_{\mathfrak C}g(x)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\mathfrak C}T^*_{\mathfrak p}g(x)$ (`adjointCarlesonSum`). e0\}$ is compact). (Lemma 7.4.6.) Let $u_1,u_2\in\mathfrak P$ with $u_1\in t$, $u_2\in t$, $u_1
e u_2$ and $\mathcal I(u_1)\le\mathcal I(u_2)$, and let $f_1,f_2:X	o\mathbb C$ be of bounded compact support.
